issuing_body: U.S. District Court, District of Minnesota; verified complaint signed on behalf of the United States and FBI agent
title: United States v. 2900 Pillsbury Avenue et al., Verified Complaint for Forfeiture In Rem, ECF 1

acquisition.channel: Free CourtListener RECAP primary filing, official district-court ECF header retained in 19-page PDF
acquisition.notes: Web tool extracted the original PDF text/page labels. The PDF screenshot endpoint returned a cache miss and container outbound DNS failed, so no binary saved or independently hashed. Source-level facts were checked against the extracted court filing, not page images.

supports: ECF 1 was filed October 19, 2026, in 0:26-cv-04533-KMM-LIB as a verified federal in-rem civil forfeiture complaint naming real properties at 2900/2906 Pillsbury Avenue and 211 West 29th Street in Minneapolis (PDF pp.1–2, paragraphs 1–3).

Paragraph 3 explicitly states the property had NOT BEEN SEIZED at filing and that the United States DID NOT request authorization to seize it 'at this time'; instead it described notice and lis pendens steps (PDF p.2). Paragraph 62 and the prayer for relief later request a warrant and ultimate forfeiture, so distinguish the present status from requested future relief (PDF pp.17–18).

Complaint paragraphs 18–25 expressly frame the alleged underlying nutrition claims through Partners in Nutrition (PIN) and the Addis Foundation; PIN is a distinct sponsor from Feeding Our Future. The complaint is the government's allegation, not judicial finding that PIN committed the described crimes (PDF pp.6–8).

Paragraphs 32–34 allege that Addis Foundation and related entities sought reimbursement of more than $13 million and claimed over 5.6 million meals across approximately 16 months in 2021–2022; these are claims alleged in the complaint, not amounts the government recovered (PDF pp.9–10).

Paragraphs 36–37 allege $796,485.60 was transferred from Addis Foundation to Fresh Point LLC on June 23, 2021 and no food services were provided during its earlier brief operation based on bank-record analysis (PDF pp.10–11).

Paragraphs 46–51 allege Fresh Point wired $400,000 toward the property and Marcon LLC closed its purchase of all three parcels July 16, 2021 for $516,058.50 including fees, funded by $10,000 earnest money, $400,000 wire, $106,000 cashier's check, $58 cash. The four listed components add to $516,058.00, $0.50 less than the complaint's stated $516,058.50 closing total in the extracted text; this unresolved discrepancy must be checked against the PDF page image and closing statement. They are not additive to the purchase price (PDF pp.13–14).
Paragraph 61 identifies Marcon LLC as known potential claimant, not a person criminally convicted in this civil action (PDF p.16).

Verification is signed under penalty of perjury by FBI Special Agent Travis Wilmer, dated October 19, 2026; the affidavit includes matters based on information and belief, not exclusively firsthand observation (PDF p.19).
does_not_support: That any person or organization named in the civil pleading has been convicted in this in-rem proceeding.
That a court found the government's tracing allegations proven or that all the cited claimed meals were never served.
That the properties had already been seized at the time of the complaint. Paragraph 3 expressly says the opposite.
That the government presently owns the property, sold the property, or recovered cash.
A final court order disposing of claimants' interests.
That the October 30 DOJ announced approximate $519,000 valuation is the July 2021 documented acquisition cost of $516,058.50; they are different figures and bases.
An independently computed PDF hash or image-level confirmation of the filing; retrieval method did not produce a local PDF binary.
An exactly reconciled component-to-total closing statement; the extracted four components are $0.50 lower than the reported price.

notes: This is the requested October 19 federal civil complaint and closes the primary text-acquisition gap. Treat all allegations as party claims, even when verified under penalty of perjury. Distinguish the complaint's PIN-sponsored alleged claims from DOJ's broader press-release wording concerning the Feeding Our Future fraud scheme. The three real properties are not the Park Avenue asset in case 22-cr-223.
